meta.title: Block Editor Creator Lab
meta.description: A modern three-part guide that teaches young creators how to build and edit posts and pages with the WordPress Block Editor.
meta.author: fellyph

options.blogdescription: Build posts and pages like a creator.

files.functions.php:
<?php
add_action( 'wp_enqueue_scripts', function() {
	wp_enqueue_style( 'block-editor-creator-lab', get_stylesheet_uri(), array(), wp_get_theme()->get( 'Version' ) );
} );

add_action( 'admin_init', function() {
	if ( ! isset( $_GET['creator_lab_challenge'] ) ) {
		return;
	}

	$challenge_id = (int) get_option( 'creator_lab_challenge_post_id' );
	if ( ! $challenge_id || ! current_user_can( 'edit_post', $challenge_id ) ) {
		return;
	}

	wp_safe_redirect( admin_url( 'post.php?post=' . $challenge_id . '&action=edit' ) );
	exit;
} );

add_action( 'template_redirect', function() {
	if ( is_admin() || ! is_front_page() ) {
		return;
	}

	wp_safe_redirect( admin_url( '?creator_lab_challenge=1' ) );
	exit;
} );

Lesson 01 / Block basics

Start a post with blocks

The Block Editor turns every idea into movable pieces: headings, images, lists, buttons, embeds, and more. Your mission is to publish a first post that feels intentional from the first block.

' . creator_lab_actions( $post_ids['start-a-post-with-blocks'] ) . '
' . creator_lab_nav( $post_ids, 'start-a-post-with-blocks' ) . '

Mission board

Four moves to publish

The reference lesson shows that posts and pages both start the same way: open the editor, add a title, then build with blocks.

Step 01

Name the idea

Go to Posts, choose Add New, and write a title that tells readers what they will get.

Step 02

Open the inserter

Use the blue plus button to browse blocks, patterns, and media options.

Step 03

Use slash commands

Type /heading, /image, or /list in the canvas when you want to add a block without breaking flow.

Step 04

Preview and publish

Preview the post, scan the structure, then publish when the page feels clear.

Try this

Build a mini intro

Stack three blocks: one Heading, one Paragraph, and one Image. Keep each block focused. You can always move or style it later.

Before you hit Publish

  • The title is specific
  • The first paragraph explains the idea
  • Each block has a clear job
  • Preview looks readable on a phone
' ); $content_two = creator_lab_quote( '

Lesson 02 / Pages and patterns

Build a page with patterns and media

Pages are for content that needs to be easy to find again. Patterns help you move faster by dropping in polished sections that you can remix.

' . creator_lab_actions( $post_ids['build-a-page-with-patterns-and-media'] ) . '
' . creator_lab_nav( $post_ids, 'build-a-page-with-patterns-and-media' ) . '

Page flow

From blank canvas to full section

The lesson highlights patterns, gallery blocks, media from the library, and Openverse as fast ways to shape a page.

Step 01

Create a page

Go to Pages, choose Add New, then write a title that sounds like a destination.

Step 02

Drop a pattern

Open the inserter, switch to Patterns, and choose a section you can edit instead of starting from zero.

Step 03

Add media

Use an Image or Gallery block, then pull from the Media Library or search Openverse for open licensed visuals.

Step 04

Tune the layout

Select the parent block, then adjust alignment, columns, spacing, and colors in the sidebar.

Use pages for

Evergreen info

About, contact, services, portfolios, and other content people return to.

Use posts for

Fresh updates

Stories, announcements, reflections, reviews, and anything that belongs in a feed.

Use patterns for

Fast structure

Ready-made sections that save time and still let you customize every block.

Creative challenge

Create a page with a heading, a two-column section, a gallery, and one button. Use the sidebar to make one design decision that changes the mood.

' ); $content_three = creator_lab_quote( '

Lesson 03 / Edit with control

Edit faster with List View and settings

When a layout grows, speed comes from knowing where you are. List View shows the full structure, the toolbar handles quick moves, and the sidebar handles deeper settings.

' . creator_lab_actions( $post_ids['edit-faster-with-list-view-and-settings'] ) . '
' . creator_lab_nav( $post_ids, 'edit-faster-with-list-view-and-settings' ) . '

Control deck

Three editor zones

The lesson separates the editor into the content area, the left side tools such as List View, and the Settings sidebar on the right.

Canvas

Build in place

Click the block you want to edit and type, replace media, or add the next block below it.

Toolbar

Fast changes

Transform blocks, drag them, move them with arrows, align text, add links, or use bold and italic.

Sidebar

Deep settings

Use block settings for styles such as columns, border radius, colors, spacing, and other block-specific controls.

Step 01

Open List View

Use the icon in the top toolbar to see every block in order, including nested groups.

Step 02

Select the parent

Choose a Group, Gallery, Columns, or Buttons block when you want to change the whole section.

Step 03

Reorder cleanly

Drag blocks in List View when the canvas is too busy or when a block is nested inside another block.

Step 04

Update the post

Preview the change, check the flow, then use Update so the public post matches your edits.

Power habit

Select first, style second

Before changing settings, confirm the block in List View. Many layout problems happen because the child block is selected when the parent block is the one that needs the change.

Challenge brief

Finish this starter post by practicing the same flow from the lessons: add blocks, shape the story, adjust settings, then publish.

  1. Replace the placeholder hook with your own opening paragraph.
  2. Add one Image or Gallery block after the intro.
  3. Use Heading blocks to create at least two clear sections.
  4. Open List View and move one block to a better position.
  5. Preview the post, then publish or update it.

My first Block Editor post

Start with a quick hook. Tell readers what this post is about and why they should keep reading.

Section one: the idea

Explain the main idea in your own voice. Keep this block focused on one point.

Section two: the visual

Add an Image or Gallery block below this paragraph. Use the sidebar to adjust its style, size, or spacing.

Use List View when you need to select, move, or understand blocks inside a bigger layout.

Make it ready to publish
